claims.text: A single-step controlled aging heat treatment can induce nanoscale precipitate formation in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The aging treatment can produce a uniform dispersion of coherent nanoscale precipitates within the HEA matrix.
Coherent precipitates act as dislocation-pinning sites.
Pinning by coherent precipitates hinders dislocation motion at high temperatures.
Hindering high-temperature dislocation motion will improve creep resistance.
Hindering high-temperature dislocation motion will improve fatigue resistance.
The treated alloy will have a lower high-temperature creep strain rate than the untreated single-phase baseline.
The treated alloy will have a longer high-temperature fatigue life than the untreated baseline.
The treatment will preserve room-temperature tensile properties relative to the untreated baseline.
The heat treatment will not increase alloy density because it does not alter the alloy's overall composition.
The proposed mechanical benefits should hold above 1000°C under creep or fatigue loading.
Aging outside an optimal temperature-time window may fail to form the desired precipitate dispersion.
Excessive aging may coarsen the precipitates and negate the mechanical benefits.
A single-step aging procedure may not fully reproduce the benefits of multi-step treatments.
